title: Headline and Core Inflation Rates in the Philippines (January 2022 – July 2024)
description: The figure shows the monthly trends of headline inflation and core inflation in the Philippines, expressed as percentage changes using 2018 as the base year (2018 = 100). Headline inflation reflects the overall price changes of goods and services, while core inflation excludes volatile items such as food and energy.

questions.text: During which period did the headline inflation rate reach its highest point according to the graph?
questions.explanation: The headline inflation curve peaks around January 2023, where it reaches its maximum value before declining.

questions.text: Which statement best describes the overall trend of the core inflation rate from January 2022 to July 2024?
questions.explanation: Core inflation generally increased until early 2023 and then showed a steady decline toward mid-2024.

choices.text: It consistently decreased throughout the period
It sharply fluctuated with no clear pattern

questions.text: In which month did the headline inflation rate fall below the core inflation rate for the first time?
questions.explanation: The graph shows the headline inflation dipping below the core inflation around August 2023.

questions.text: Which of the following months shows the smallest gap between headline and core inflation rates?
questions.explanation: The two lines are closest around July 2023, indicating the smallest difference between the two rates.

questions.text: Based on the graph, which inference is most reasonable?
questions.explanation: The graph suggests inflation pressures eased after early 2023, as both headline and core inflation trended downward.

choices.text: Inflation continued to rise steadily after 2023
Core inflation is always higher than headline inflation
Headline inflation remained unchanged throughout the period
